messages:
sam: FYI customer hitting repeated MFA prompts after we rotated the session cookie yesterday. They say every API request prompts reauth.
jess: ack. which customer and env? any error codes in their app?
sam: AcmePilot on prod-us-east. App logs show 401s and then an immediate Set-Cookie with a new __rf_session value on every response. snippet: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized\nSet-Cookie: __rf_session=abc123; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly` then next request `Set-Cookie: __rf_session=def456` etc.
ingrid: evidence of cookie rotation on every auth attempt. Could be KMS rekeying session encryption or a bug in session affinity. Do we have deploys around 2123999000-2124005000?
session-bot: deploy-notifier: rolled out service/auth-service@v3.14.2 to prod-us-east at 2124001200 by ops-bot.
ryan: I pulled Okta logs for AcmePilot: their SAML response looks valid, but our session-store shows a transient skip in lookup after write — reads are hitting the old key and code treats as invalid and issues new cookie. Repro steps incoming.
jess: can we get a minimal curl that reproduces? customer says it happens from their mobile web + embedded SDK.
sam: repro (from a node: server side):
```
curl -v -c /tmp/cookiejar -b /tmp/cookiejar -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# do it twice, note Set-Cookie header changes and second request returns 401
```
ingrid: thanks. that pattern matches a race: write returns new cookie but subsequent request uses it before it has been fully propagated to the session read path (replica lag + immediate read). If auth-service treats missing lookup as expired -> forces reauth and issues new cookie.
ryan: adding logs: `auth-service` shows "session_lookup: miss, creating new session id" for the same client ip within <500ms. Replica lag measured ~200-300ms during spike.
marta: customer-facing workaround: ask them to retry after 1s or enable sticky session to the auth-service instance for now (we can instruct their load balancer). Also ask them to pin cookie domain to `.redwood.example.com` if they have cross-subdomain.
sam: customer needs an immediate fix — retries are not ideal. Any quick server-side mitigations?
ingrid: short-term patch: when we write a new session we can return a trace header and accept either the previous id or the newly issued id for 2 seconds during propagation. I'll prepare a canary.
ryan: created a branch `auth/accept-transient-session` and deployed to prod-us-east canary. I also toggled read-after-write allowance = 2s.
session-bot: canary-deploy: auth-service-canary v3.14.3 -> prod-us-east (10% traffic) at 2124009800.
marta: please add a kb note for support: steps to advise customers and which services we modified.
ryan: tests: ran the curl loop 50x, previously 100% 401 on second request, after canary 98% pass (2% still hit depending on replica lag).
jess: good, escalate to SRE to monitor replica lag and consider sync options. Also flag for next-day postmortem.
sam: logged a support ticket with AcmePilot, shared the temporary workaround and ETA for a full fix.
ingrid: plan: (1) keep acceptance window for 48h, (2) instrument a histogram for session read latency, (3) evaluate persistent session-store leader reads.
marta: thanks team. I'll create an incident and notify account exec. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks — will follow up with customer once we confirm stabilizing metrics.
